**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Lewis calls this set-it-and-forget-it: barring something ridiculous enough to wreck many other futures on these three programmes, he is backing the sport's top teams to do their job and reach the playoff. On Ohio State he cites returning elite talent in Heisman hopefuls Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin, giving Ryan Day a chance at a better overall team than last year's, and adds that the Buckeyes' Over 9.5 team total is a solid foundational future in its own right. On Notre Dame he argues that Marcus Freeman's programme staying independent, and so avoiding a potential SEC or Big Ten gauntlet, is an enormous advantage.

*Rests on:* returning talent (Smith, Sayin); coaching (Day, Freeman); Notre Dame's independence and the resulting schedule

*Conflict or ambiguity:* This is the feature's only parlay and resolves to no single team, so it is filed under a parlay market rather than assigned to one programme.

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Lewis calls Lane Kiffin's arrival in Baton Rouge arguably the most compelling storyline in college football, not just the SEC. He points to a roster overhauled through the portal alongside significant NIL investment, and argues year one under Kiffin usually brings drastic improvement, especially on offense. He expects quarterback Sam Leavitt to run a high-octane attack with fresh receiver transfers around him — big-play threats Jayce Brown from Kansas State and Jackson Harris from Hawaii, plus Winnie Watkins, who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss — and reads the schedule as favourable.

*Rests on:* coaching (Kiffin, year one); portal overhaul and NIL investment; quarterback (Leavitt); schedule
